1. 1. This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual /Physical Mode).
2. Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner as well as learned Additional Standing Counsel for the State.
Perused the records.

3. This is an application under Section 482 BNSS, 2023 filed by the Petitioner for anticipatory bail,
involving offence punishable under Section 137(2) of B.N.S., 2023.
4. Learned counsel for the Petitioner at the outset contended that the Petitioner and the victim were in a love relationship.
He further contended that the aforesaid information came to the knowledge of the family members of the victim, as a result of which the victim was subjected to mental torture by her family members.
Thereafter the victim called the present Petitioner and fled away with him on her own volition without being pressured or coerced by the present Petitioner.
Learned counsel for the Petitioner further submitted that the Petitioner is innocent and he has not kidnapped the victim in this case.

He further submitted that the Petitioner has not kept any physical relationship with the victim during the aforesaid period and that in the meantime the victim has been rescued and she has been staying with her parents in the meantime.

On such ground, learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner, who is a poor innocent boy be enlarged on bail on such terms and conditions as would be deemed just and proper by this Court.

5. Learned Additional Standing counsel for the State on the other hand while objecting to the release of the Petitioner on bail submitted that the allegation made in the F.I.R. is of grave and serious in nature.
He also contended that the victim is a minor girl aged about 15 years.
It is also contended that since the investigation is on, release of the Petitioner at this juncture would further cause delay in conclusion of investigation.
It is also possibility of the Petitioner to influence the prosecution witnesses.
On such ground, learned Additional Standing Counsel objected to the release of the Petitioner on pre- arrest bail.

6. Perused the Case Diary as well as the statement of the victim recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C.
by the learned J.M.F.C., Banarpal.

On perusal of the statement under section 164 Cr.P.C. which is a part of the Case Diary, it appears that the victim has categorically stated before the leaned magistrate that her family members after knowing her relationship with the Petitioner scolded her and subjected to mental harassment, as a result of which the victim informed the Petitioner and fled away with him.
She has stated further in her statement under section 164 Cr.P.C. that after they left the parental house of the victim and stayed in a forest.
She has categorically stated that two days after they fled way from the village.
The Petitioner dropped her in her village and during the aforesaid stay in the forest with the Petitioner, the Petitioner has not kept any physical relationship forcibly with the victim.
The statement of the victim obviously means that there was no physical relationship between the two during the aforesaid period.

7. Taking into consideration the statement of the victim and the fact that the victim requested the Petitioner to take her away from her parental house and during the aforesaid period, she has not kept any physical relationship with the Petitioner, this Court is of the prima facie view that a case under section 376 of the Indian Penal Code is not made out strictly on the basis of the materials collected so far.

Keeping in view the aforesaid facts and circumstances, the Petitioner is directed to surrender and move an application for bail before the learned J.M.F.C., Banarpal in G.R.Case No.639 of 2024 arising out of Banarpal P.S.Case No.278 of 2024 within a period of three weeks from today.

In such eventuality, learned court in seisin over the matter shall do well to release the Petitioner on bail on such terms and conditions as the learned Magistrate may deem just and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case.
